  Tuesday, August 27, 2019
  6:30 P.M.

LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  August 27, 2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Mayor
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Eric Podley, BUSD
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Morgan Kostolefsky, Resident
  Kristin Charlebois, Resident
  Vanessa Hess, Resident
  Kim Svatos, Resident
  David Svatos, Resident
  Krista Chakmak, Resident
  Michael Gaydos, BHS Representative
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Jamie Ritchey, Tri-City
  Isela Moreno, Tri-City
  April Fousz, American Lung Association
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Association
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the May meeting were approved.

4. POA Fundraiser  This item was postponed to a future meeting.

5. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  noted that the school year was under way and there
  had been some incidents that required his
  involvement. SRO Cambero reminded the group
  about the dangers of vaping and that there recently
  was a death likely related to vaping. The group
  discussed further outreach and opportunities to
  educate the community on these issues.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes August 27, 2019, page 2

6. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  (BUSD) provided an update on the new
  counselors/mental health professionals now in
  schools. Mark also informed the group of new
  leadership at La Verne Heights and Ramona as well
  as the BUSD’s focus for the upcoming year. Mark
  lastly provided information on an upcoming Parent
  Partnership Academy taking place on October 12th.

  Eric Podley with BUSD provided an update on the
  Glenn Davis Stadium construction.

7. Executive Board Opening  Bill Aguirre with the City of La Verne informed the
  group that there was now an opening on the YFAC
  Executive Board. Mayor Kendrick nominated Denise
  Fisher which was seconded by Council Member
  Carder. Denise was approved unanimously by the
  Executive Board and the recommendation will now go
  to the City Council for approval.

8. Summer Lunch Program  Bill provided an update on this year’s Summer Lunch
  Program. 832 children and 316 adults participated.
  The group discussed possible reasons for the overall
  numbers being lower than previous years.

9. Video Updates  JR Ranells with the City of La Verne shared the Mental
  Health themed video that had been created and put
  out on social media earlier in the month. The group
  also discussed several different options for future
  videos including Every 15 Minutes/underage drinking,
  pharmaceuticals, marijuana, vaping/nicotine, opioids,
  school shootings etc... JR will coordinate the ideas
  and possibly make into a combination video covering
  multiple topics. Denise also suggested a video on the
  CTEC programs and Mayor Kendrick noted that he
  would assist with that video.

10. American Lung Assoc.  Jessica Vozella and April Fousz with the American
  Lung Association introduced their organization to the
  group. They are working in the La Verne area on
  issues such as health risks associated with vaping.
  Jessica is working directly with the Police Department,
  schools, and area city councils.

11. Round Table  Isela Moreno with Tri-City Mental Health provided
  information on the upcoming Stakeholders Meeting.
  Hollie Savage with the Police Department shared
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes August 27, 2019, page 3

  ideas on utilizing Instagram with shorter
  videos/messaging to inform the community on
  important topics. Hollie also noted that the Public
  Safety Open House will be taking place on Saturday,
  November 2nd.

  SRO Cambero discussed the impact of mental health
  issues on a community and police officers.

  Bill shared that the City had applied for a grant to
  assist with funding the Teen Center construction.

  Carolyn Cockrell noted issues surrounding youth cell
  phone use and tools that parents might be able to take
  advantage of.

  David Yim with Tri-City shared information on the
  Counseling Program and that work was underway with
  the beginning of school.

  Jamie Ritchey shared information on upcoming events
  regarding mental health stigma reduction and suicide
  prevention.

  Kristin Charlebois shared that she has a child entering
  middle school and that it would be beneficial for the
  group to explore doing a regular “parent tip” on topics
  of interest.

  Morgan Kostolefsky noted that attendees should also
  invite friends and neighbors so additional people can
  participate in YFAC and receive the information
  discussed.

  Vanessa Hess informed the group that she was willing
  to assist students by sharing her personal story and
  experiences with mental health.

  Krista Chakmak suggested that the YFAC videos be
  played at public places such as the Teen Center and
  library. Krista also praised the Police Departments
  presence around the schools during the last couple of
  weeks.

  Denise provided an update on the K9 Committee and
  future fundraising efforts.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes August 27, 2019, page 4

  Matt Lyons shared information about the upcoming
  Smudge Pot football game between Bonita High
  School and San Dimas High School.

  Council Member Carder shared information about
  La Verne Day at the Fair.

  Mayor Kendrick thanked the group for attending and
  generating the informative and productive discussions.

12.  Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for September
  24, 2019 at 6:30 p.m.

13. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 8:30 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
